subject: FluxRetail renewal: milestone discount smoothing & staged capacity uplift
messages:
From: Asha Rao <asha@fluxretail.com>

Cc: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@fluxretail.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Jan 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal planning — smoothing discounts around seasonal uplift

Hi Monica,

Hope you had a good break. Our fiscal Q2 looks like it will include a large promotional push and we expect peak inference consumption for ~8 weeks. We want to lock a renewal that:
- holds a predictable blended unit price across the year (smoothing our Q2 spike),
- gives FluxRetail staged uplift capacity that scales with milestones (not a single one-time commit),
- includes a short-term price hold if we sign by end of Jan.

Can you share a term structure that avoids a big upfront commit but still gives us meaningful discounts tied to milestones? I attached last quarter's usage for context.

Thanks — would prefer a short call next week if helpful.

—Asha

[Attachment: usage_dash_q4.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>

Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@fluxretail.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — smoothing discounts around seasonal uplift

Hi Asha — thanks for the context and the dashboard. I copied Vivek (sales lead) so we can align commercial and ops. High level proposal we can offer:

1) Staged uplift commits: three milestone tranches (25% / 50% / 100% of target uplift) tied to calendar milestones you define; each tranche unlocks a ~6% incremental discount on the uplifted units.
2) Blended smoothing: we’ll offer a blended unit price calculation across the contract year that amortizes uplift discounts over 12 months (protects you from a big Q2 spike billing).
3) Price hold: 90-day price hold on the blended price if signed by 31 Jan.
4) Overage guard: temporary burst credit pool for the first 60 days after each milestone (to avoid surprise charges during promo ramp).

I attached a draft term sheet with figures mapped to your Q4 usage. We kept the upfront financial commitment modest and instead use milestone and usage triggers.

Proposed next step: 30-min sync Wed (13th) to walk the term sheet and confirm milestone dates. If that works I’ll loop in legal to prepare a DocuSign addendum.

Best,
Monica Patel
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Hi team — following the walkthrough earlier today, a couple operational notes to capture in the addendum so we avoid surprises:

- True-up mechanics: we’ll recalculate the blended price at the annual true-up. If final uplift < last milestone, we prorate discounts and apply a one-time true-up invoice (or credit) to align billing. This protects both sides and keeps monthly invoices stable.
- Burst credits: credits are tagged as non-milestone consumption; they will not count toward tranche unlocks.
- Model changes: price hold covers equivalent model variants listed in the term sheet (we’ll enumerate families/quantization profiles in the DocuSign addendum). Material architecture changes will be handled as a separate change order.
- Ops request: please confirm target milestone dates in the HubSpot record so we can provision staged capacity ahead of your promo.

I attached the usage snapshot and updated term sheet appendix with the true-up language added. Legal flagged one small language tweak for the price-hold clause — I’ll send that in the DocuSign for sign-off.

Thanks — Steph

Redwood Inference
